DISPLACED
PERSONS (LAND SETTLEMENT)
RULES, 1959
S. R. O, 392, 17th August 1959,
(Gazette Extraordinary, 24th August 1959).‑In exercise of the powers
conferred by section 3‑1 of the Displaced Persons (Land Settlement Act,
19m (XLVll of 1958) the Central Government is pleased to make the following
rules, namely :‑----
1. Short title.‑These rules may be called the Displaced
Persons (Land Settlement) Rules, 1959. '
2. Definitions.‑In these rules,‑
(a) "the
Act" means the Displaced Persons (Land Settlement) Act, 1958 (XLVII of
1958) ; and
(b) "section" means a section of the Act.
3. Seal.‑Every Settlement Authority shall have
a seal bearing the designation of the officer concerned and name of the place
where his head quarters are situates.
4. Compensation
Pool.‑For the purpose of granting compensation to displaced persons
whose claims have been verified, there shall be only one compensation pool
consisting of all land proceeds, rent, profits, incomes and amounts referred to
in section 5.
5. Ejectment.‑The
procedure for ejectment under subsection (3) of section 11 shall be as
follows, namely :‑
(a) The Settlement Authority shall, in the first
instance, issue a notice to the person concerned to show cause, within such
period, not being less than seven days as it may specify in the notice why he
should not be ejected ;
(b) After
considering the representation, if any, made by or on behalf of the person
concerned and after taking such evidence as it may consider necessary, the
Settlement Authority may mane an order raider subsection (3) of section 11
which shall be served in the manner prescribed in rule 6 ;
(c) If the person on whom an
order under clause (b) has been served fails to deliver possession of the
property to the Settlement Authority within seven days of the service of the
order, the Settlement Authority may direct that the person be ejected with the
use of such force as may be necessary.
6. Service of
Notice, etc.‑(1) Service of any notice, summons or order issued or
made under the Act shall be effected in one or more of the following modes,
namely :‑
(a) by delivering or tendering the notice, summons or
order to the person on whom it is intended to be served, or his agent, if any ;
(b) by
leaving it at the last known place of business or residence of such person or
delivering or tendering it to some adult member of his family ;
(c) by transmitting it by registered post to such
person at the address of the last known place of his business or residence ;
(d) by affixing it at Some conspicuous place in or
near the premises con?cerned or the last known place of business or residence
of such person;
(e) by
publication in a newspaper. or proclamation by beat of drum or other customary
method in the locality;
(2) Service under clause (b) or clause (d) or sub‑rule (1) shall be effected in the
presence of two respectable persons residing in the locality.
7. Permanent
settlement on land.‑In pursuance of the provisions of subsection (31
w section 15, a displaced person to whom any land has been allotted b;
Rehabilitation Authority under a scheme as defined in clause (7) of section 2
or by a Settlement Authority under subsection (1) of section 15, shall be
permanently settled on that land in the manner, subject to the follow?ing terms
and conditions and payment of settlement fees prescribed in rule 10 :‑
(i) After the acquisition of the land under section 4
and the constitution of the Compensation Pool under section 5, the Assistant

to subsection (3) of section 15,‑

a mutation of extinction of all evacuee
rights and interests in the entire estate

for the evacuee holders of rights in the estate ; and
